To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of tamoxifen for the prevention of breast cancer is associated with an increased incidence of endometrial cancer.

the expression of ER and PR in the tumor is associated with a decreased risk of recurrence in patients with early breast cancer, while the expression of HER-2 in the tumor is not associated with an increased risk of recurrence in this population.

1) the use of the aromatase inhibitor, letrozole, in the adjuvant treatment of postmenopausal women with early breast cancer is associated with a statistically significant improvement in DFS, 2) the use of anastrozole is associated with a similar improvement in DFS, and 3) there is no difference in the magnitude of the DFS benefit with letrozole compared with anastrozole.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new class of drugs for the treatment of cancer and other diseases.
the study of the effects of the chemical structure on the properties of the compounds.
the development of new methods for the synthesis of novel compounds and the study of their biological activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results of these studies suggest that tamoxifen is effective in preventing breast cancer and that the risk reduction increases with time.

, the use of aromatase inhibitors is associated with a higher risk of developing cardiovascular events, but this is outweighed by the benefits in terms of reduced recurrence rates and improved survival.

, in the ATAC trial, there is a statistically significant association between the presence of ER-positive and/or PgR-positive tumors and improved disease-free and overall survival, and that the presence of both ER and PgR is the best predictor of survival.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression level of ER, PR and HER2 is a significant predictor for the response and recurrence of breast cancer.

the results of the ATAC study are consistent with those from previous adjuvant trials of endocrine therapy, and the addition of anastrozole to tamoxifen did not provide any benefit in overall survival, but did reduce recurrence and contralateral disease.
there is an important role for epidermal growth element receptors in the regulation of cell proliferation and survival.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the expression of the HER2 receptor is associated with the response of the tumor to endocrine therapies and with the development of endocrine resistance in the long term, and that this association may be mediated by a mechanism that is independent of the PIK3CA mutation status, which is the most common oncogenic alteration in breast tumors.

the expression of estrogen and progester-one receptors is associated with HER-2 expression and that the combination of HER-2 and ER expression is a better predictor of outcome than HER-2 expression alone.
we can now use a simple, inexpensive and noninvasive test to predict the response of patients to hormone therapy.
